exposure: Preeclamptic pregnant women vs. normal pregnant women
cohort: 150 pregnant women (75 with preeclampsia and 75 normal pregnancies)
finding: Serum SHARP1 levels were significantly higher in preeclamptic women compared to normal pregnant women, and preeclampsia was associated with a higher rate of cesarean section, lower neonatal birth weight, and increased neonatal complications.
mod_finding: Preeclamptic women had a higher rate of cesarean section compared to normal pregnant women (68% vs. 32%, p < .001).
birth_weight: Neonatal birth weight was lower in preeclamptic women (2,546.1 ± 766.3g vs 2,884.5 ± 499.9g, p = .001)
